There was another period when the Chetniks had calmed down some of their forces on the battlefield and it was possible that these forces, together with HVO forces, might exert even greater pressure on 3rd Corps units. If that had happened, it would have been even more catastrophic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since I see the time -- I have another ten minutes -- I need another ten minutes for this witness. I could continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll continue tomorrow. So you will have to return tomorrow for the hearing that commences at 9.00. You shouldn't see anyone in the meantime. Since you have taken a solemn declaration, you are now a witness testifying in the interests of justice. Please come back at 9.00 tomorrow. Is there anything that the Prosecution would like to say? Ms. Benjamin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, with the permission of the Court. My learned friend uses documents that were not on the list she provided at about 1.30 yesterday afternoon. And for the record, it just throws my cross-examination preparation off. At least three of the documents so far that have been used are documents that have been taken by surprise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Apparently the Prosecution is objecting to the fact that you are using documents that weren't disclosed to them, 633 I assume is one of the documents. Which are the documents that are in dispute? What are the numbers of these documents on the list?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: DH1296 is not on the list. DH1298 is not on the list. And, of course, P599 and P271 are already in evidence so I suppose she can use those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Defence counsel, apparently you did not disclose documents 1296 and 1298.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in accordance with the suggestion you made and the practice followed to date, we provided the Prosecution with the numbers of the documents that are not in evidence. All the documents referred to by my learned friend are documents that have been admitted into evidence. The Prosecution is familiar with this material. And to make it easier to follow the proceedings, we provided everyone with copies of these documents of these this morning. So these are documents that are in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution, apparently the Prosecution is familiar with these documents because document 1296 and document 1298 have already been used. You're supposed to be familiar with them, as well as the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, firstly, the documents were just handed to us a while ago. And if in fact that we are supposed to be familiar with them, at least we should be -- we should be told what was going to be used so at least we could familiarise ourselves again with it. And the documents that were distributed to us a while ago. We weren't aware that these documents were going to be used. The 65 ter statement is just three lines long, and the way that the statement is phrased, there was no indication or any indication was given that these documents could have been used with respect to what's in that statement there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you have raised a problem I have already mentioned. Unfortunately, I'll have to mention this problem to the Defence again. In the course of the Prosecution's case, the Prosecution always mentioned the documents that would be used to support their examination-in-chief. The rules for the Prosecution are the same for Defence counsel. The rules are the same for both parties. So when Defence counsel presents a list of a witness they will be calling, on a number of occasions I have asked Defence counsel to attach to this list documents that will be used when witnesses appear, a list of such documents. For a few weeks when receiving lists of witnesses but reference is never made to documents. So why are Defence counsel proceeding in this manner since the Prosecution always made an effort to state which documents would be used; whereas, you are not making this effort. You are a party that has the same obligations as the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have been providing the Prosecution with a list of documents that we intend to use if they are not in evidence. That's what we took your decision to mean. If you suggest that we should also disclose and provide other documents, well, I saw the witness yesterday and then I decided which documents would be used. Before -- prior to that, I provided the Prosecution with a broad list of documents and said that I would finally decide on documents used after I had proofed the witness. I know that for the last two months of their case the Prosecution provided us with documents, but we have been making attempts from the beginning of our case to provide not only numbers of documents but also copies of documents to facilitate the work for everyone in the courtroom. This is in the interest of the defence for my client and this is how we have been proceeding. If the Chamber believes that we should provide the same list that we provide to the Prosecution to the Chamber as well, we will by all means do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Defence counsel says that the Prosecution has been provided with information of all these documents. But since it was only yesterday that Defence counsel proofed the witness, they were not in a position to know which documents they would be using until the very last moment. As a result, it's only during the hearing that they provided a list of the documents. But the Defence also added that the Prosecution is supposed to be familiar with all these documents and information has been provided to the Prosecution about these documents already. The only difference between your positions is that when the Prosecution called a witness, there was already a witness statement; they had already met on a number of occasions with the witnesses. Whereas, the Defence counsel is not really in the same situation. Ms. Benjamin, what would you say about the matter? And then the Judges will instruct the parties as to how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is just a little bit odd to me that the Defence would expect that because documents were before the -- the Court at an earlier stage that the Prosecution by some magic should be able to know what documents are going to be used with this witness for preparation of cross-examination. Aside from that, I am very much aware that the Defence may be proofing their witnesses late in the evening or whatever. But certainly I think it would be most kind of the Prosecution -- of the Defence if they could at least alert us before we come in here with the ones that they want to use and -- and let us know that the ones that they have on the list, that they're not using those. Because it -- it enables us to guide our cross-examination in a certain way. Certainly me. Because when I look at the ter statement, I take a certain course. And then when I'm coming here, I'm presented with an element of surprise. And I don't think that could be -- could be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As we will be continuing with the hearing of this witness tomorrow, you'll have time to examine the documents and to conduct an efficient cross-examination. We'll -- we, the Judges, will discuss the matter in general terms and tell you how one should proceed tomorrow. The registrar has said that the courtroom is needed after 2.00, so we will now have to adjourn. Thank you. And I will see everyone tomorrow at the hearing that shall start at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, 20th day of January, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.58 p.m.,
